bodyAggregateNote.value:
Each body metric is a single value from the latest export — never an average over a
window. Values are summarised as ranges, shares, or goal status rather than published
raw. This document links no raw health values; the public data API is documented at
{siteUrl}/developers.

The former {bodyEndingDate} substitution is REDUNDANT, not wrong. LP render.ts binds bodyDataAsOf from the same view.body.dataAsOf value, and full.bodyDataAsOf already publishes it one line earlier as '**Data as of:** {bodyDataAsOf}', so the note was restating a date the document states above it. (Historical note for anyone re-deriving this: before LP PR #356 the binding WAS the compose instant — view.ts endingDate: formatDate(inputs.composedAt) — and the reason to drop it was that it could not honestly date the values at all. #356 repointed it at the health export's own date, so the honesty objection is gone and only the duplication remains.) errorsBody.value: Every 4xx and 5xx response under /api/v1, and the 404 for any other unknown /api path, is an RFC 9457 problem document, served as application/problem+json. Its members are type, title, status, detail, and instance. The type URI points at the matching entry below, a fragment of this page. Some problem types add extension members, and their entries name them.

_meta.description: Section body — the error model: every 4xx and 5xx under /api, the /api/v1 paths and the 404 for any other unknown /api path, answers application/problem+json with the five RFC 9457 members. The type URI is {siteUrl}/developers#problem-<slug>; each slug has an entry built from a problem*Title and problem*Detail key in this group.

_meta.description: Section heading — the /api/v1 versioning and deprecation policy.
_meta.rationale: Atlas decision 0158 follow-on, plan is-agentic-api-v1 step 1 (owner approval 2026-10-24). The website /api/v1 facade adopts this key in the PR that ships the routes, pinned to this copy release.

versioningBody.value: The path carries the major version: v1. Within a version, response schemas only gain optional members. A removed member or a changed type ships as a new path version, and the old version keeps answering for at least 90 days. During that period its responses carry the Deprecation and Sunset headers and a Link header with rel="successor-version". A major release of the portal contract that removes or retypes an export member triggers a new version.

_meta.description: Section body — the versioning promise: path versioning, additive-only change within a version, a support window of at least 90 days for the old version with RFC 9745 Deprecation, RFC 8594 Sunset, and Link rel="successor-version", and the trigger (a portal-contract major that removes or retypes an export member). The website OpenAPI info.description restates it.
_meta.rationale: Atlas decision 0158 follow-on, plan is-agentic-api-v1 step 1 (owner approval 2026-10-24). The website /api/v1 facade adopts this key in the PR that ships the routes, pinned to this copy release. The "90 days" is a support window, not a data window: llm-claim-honesty.test.ts exempts this leaf from its N-day pattern by name.

_meta.description: Section heading — the /api/v1 rate-limit policy.
_meta.rationale: Atlas decision 0158 follow-on, plan is-agentic-api-v1 step 1 (owner approval 2026-10-24). The website /api/v1 facade adopts this key in the PR that ships the routes, pinned to this copy release.

rateLimitBody.value: Each client gets 60 requests per minute. Every response from an export path under /api/v1 carries the RateLimit-Policy header field from the IETF httpapi draft, and every response the counter counted also carries the RateLimit header field. If the counter is unavailable, the request is still served and the RateLimit field is absent. A 429 response also carries Retry-After. The limit is a courtesy budget for a free, read-only API.

_meta.description: Section body — the rate-limit policy: 60 requests per 60-second window per client (the website API_V1_RATE_LIMIT constant), the draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers fields RateLimit-Policy ("default";q=60;w=60) on every response from an export path under /api/v1, RateLimit ("default";r=<remaining>;t=<seconds>) on every response the counter counted, and Retry-After on a 429. The facade fails open: when the counter is unreachable it serves the request and omits RateLimit, because it has no honest r or t to state; RateLimit-Policy stays, since the policy does not depend on the counter. The facade checks the path and the method before the limit (plan Design, Request handling), so a 404 or 405 does not carry the fields; the value is scoped to export paths for that reason.
_meta.rationale: Atlas decision 0158 follow-on, plan is-agentic-api-v1 step 1 (owner approval 2026-10-24). The website /api/v1 facade adopts this key in the PR that ships the routes, pinned to this copy release. Changed 2026-10-24 (website #395 review, finding M2): the value promised RateLimit on every export response, but the facade omits it when the counter is unreachable.

_meta.description: Section heading — the read-only MCP server.

mcpBody.value: {siteUrl}/mcp is a read-only Model Context Protocol server over stateless Streamable HTTP. Its resources are llms-full.txt and every JSON export except health, sleep, and workouts, which reach agents only as the coarsened bands in llms-full.txt. Its tools return the profile, the data sources, current reading, and the tech stack. No session, no authentication. The server card is at {siteUrl}/mcp/server-card.

_meta.description: Section heading — focus-mode suppression.

focusBody.value: Some focus modes hide the public data. While one is active, the CloudFront data host answers each JSON export except focus.json with HTTP 403 and a JSON body that states suppressed: true and carries no data. Under /api/v1 the same exports answer HTTP 503 with a focus-suppressed problem document and a Retry-After header. The on-domain llms.txt, llms-full.txt, index.md, and feeds answer HTTP 503 with a Retry-After header. The MCP server withholds the same data. focus.json publishes the current state. Wait and retry; do not route around the gate.

_meta.description: Section body — the fail-closed focus gate: the 403 the CloudFront data host returns for each suppressible JSON export (mantle-LifegamesPortal src/edge/focus-gate.js SUPPRESSION_RESPONSE), the 503 focus-suppressed problem document the /api/v1 facade returns for the same exports, the 503 with Retry-After the website proxy returns for its other on-domain routes (src/lib/edge/proxy.ts makeCloudfrontProxy), and the instruction not to bypass the gate.
_meta.rationale: Changed 2026-10-24 (plan is-agentic-api-v1 step 1): the developers page links the /api/v1 paths, which answer a focus-suppressed 503, so the body names both hosts. The 403 sentence still holds for the CloudFront URLs, which the MCP resources keep.
